transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-03-14 16:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Location: Zoom (recording)
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood CSM), Luis Romero (Redwood SE), Alicia Torres (Silverstrand Head of MLOps), Derek Wu (Silverstrand Platform Eng), Priya Shah (Silverstrand GRC)

Summary:
Quick kickoff to align on onboarding, governance, and pilot scope for Silverstrand Health's Redwood Private deployment. Covered network topology (VPC peering), compliance (SOC2, data residency), tenant provisioning, pilot success metrics, and initial timeline. Agreed on runbook delivery, security questionnaire, and staging tenant provisioning as immediate next steps.

Topics:
- Goals & timeline
- Security / compliance / SSO
- Network / VPC peering and firewall rules
- Staging tenant & model routing (dedicated vs hosted variants)
- Success metrics and pilot acceptance
- Next steps and owners

Transcript Body:
00:00 Jordan: alright team thanks for joining, um I'm Jordan from Redwood, i'll kick us off briefly, we sent the agenda, hope that's okay.
00:18 Alicia: yup thanks Jordan, quick context — we're looking to move inference for our patient-notes summarization pipeline into a private setup, low latency is critical, also strict residency, so SSO and audit logs are must haves.
00:34 Maya: yeah hi all, i'm Maya on the CS side, we'll own the delivery and runbook, and coordinate with Luis on the infra bits.
00:45 Derek: quick note — our infra already runs in us-east-1, we want to avoid cross-region routing, also our security team asked about envelope encryption + K M S integration.
01:02 Luis: hey, Luis — on the SE side I'll handle the staging tenant and routing, curious about how Redwood handles KV cache warmup and batching, we have variable sequence lengths which break naive batching.
01:20 Jordan: good call — the runtime has workload-aware batching and prefix caching, though sometimes the transcription shows K V cash, sorry, but functionally we do prefix / KV caching and the engines pick quantization profiles per model.
01:37 Priya: can you repeat the SOC2 part? our audit requires evidence of log retention and separation of customer data.
01:45 Jordan: sure, Redwood Private supports audit logs, per-tenant retention policies; we can export logs to your SIEM or S3, and we support KMS integration so keys are customer-managed.
01:58 Alicia: when you say export, is that a push or do we pull? we have strict pull-only rules for some environments.
02:06 Luis: currently we can push encrypted logs to your S3; we also have an endpoint for your SIEM to pull — depends on your preference.
02:17 Derek: firewall rules — what ports and egress do we need to enable for the peering?
02:24 Maya: we'll share a network checklist; broadly it's TLS outbound for control plane, and gRPC over 443 for runtime; sometimes customers host a small NAT egress for patches.
02:38 Alicia: service accounts and RBAC — we need role separation between dev and clinical teams.
02:45 Jordan: Redwood Console supports RBAC and SSO via SAML, you can map groups to roles and we emit token-level audit trails for all model calls.
02:58 Priya: what about data residency — how do you ensure patient data never leaves our VPC?
03:05 Luis: with Redwood Private we deploy inference runtime into your VPC or on-prem nodes; all payloads stay in your network, only metadata needed for control plane (if you opt in) goes to Redwood control plane — and we can run with a private control plane option per contract.
03:22 Alicia: ok that sounds promising. can we do a short perf benchmark — latency target is p95 < 120ms for 512 tokens?
03:30 Jordan: yes, we can run a perf benchmark in staging. typical numbers vary by model and instance type; we'll propose a hardware baseline in the runbook.
03:41 Derek: curious on model variants: for cost reasons we might route lower-priority flows to quantized variants or a cheaper family. how seamless is falling back?
03:51 Luis: runtime supports automatic fallback to compatible model variants; you declare routing policies, e.g., latency-first vs cost-first, and the router will select accordingly. sometimes names get butchered in transcripts — like 'Redwood Optimize' — but that's our cost/perf toolkit.
04:10 Alicia: timeline — we have an internal board and need pilot by end of April. is that realistic?
04:17 Maya: yes it's tight but doable if we get network details & questionnaire back this week; plan: runbook + staging tenant by 3/22, perf run 3/24-3/28, pilot validation week of 4/12.
04:34 Priya: on security questionnaire — do you provide a filled sample? we prefer to see patterns vs generic answers.
04:40 Jordan: we'll complete the questionnaire with environment-specific notes; Maya will own it.
04:47 Derek: about traffic shaping — we've got bursts during nightly ingestion windows, can Redwood handle bursts without violating latency SLOs?
04:56 Luis: we can configure reserved capacity on Dedicated pools for predictable throughput and autoscale for bursts. we'll recommend a reserved baseline and burst buffer.
05:10 Alicia: any constraints around model tokenization or special tokens — we use a mix of clinical shorthand and lots of long tokens.
05:18 Luis: tokenizer compatibility depends on model; we'll test with your sample prompts. also KV cache helps with prefix-heavy workloads.
05:29 Priya: is there an SSO metadata upload we need to provide now?
05:33 Maya: yes, send SAML metadata and prod/test entity IDs; we'll configure a test SSO flow in staging.
05:40 Jordan: quick recaps — immediate items: Jordan send runbook & quickstart; Maya send questionnaire stub filled; Luis create staging tenant; Derek provide VPC details; Priya return questionnaire and NDA.
05:58 Alicia: sounds good, thanks everyone. can we schedule the peering deep-dive next Mon?
06:03 Jordan: yep added to next steps — we'll propose two slots and lock one.
06:10 Derek: one more — any PCI/PHI-specific guidance for logs retention?
06:14 Priya: that's actually mine, we'll coordinate offline with Maya and Jordan.
06:20 Jordan: great, i'll share a summary and the runbook after this call. thanks all.

End of recording.
